GH-803: hoist repeated linked-test execution context and honor lean output

pm test --run --json repeats a 16-field sandbox execution_context on every result even though the context is invocation-scoped; in the reported one-test case it consumes 727 of 1,301 bytes and grows redundantly with each linked test.
Issue
open
harness:codex

Invocation-scoped execution context is emitted once rather than duplicated on every linked-test result, with no diagnostic information loss; Lean structured output omits non-actionable successful-run sandbox plumbing while failures retain enough provenance to diagnose context isolation; Default and full projections remain explicitly contracted and backward compatibility is handled through a documented schema/version strategy; CLI, SDK, MCP, JSON schemas, contracts, and documentation expose one consistent test-run output shape; Measured multi-test output proves a material byte and token reduction while focused and exact 100 percent coverage remain green
project management = context management
Pay once for invocation provenance and reserve per-result output for result-specific evidence
Agents retain more context for actionable test failures and project decisions
Removes multiplicative payload overhead from linked-test sweeps without discarding sandbox diagnostics
Structured linked-test output scales with useful results rather than repeated temporary-path plumbing
GH-803 measured execution_context at 56 percent of a passing one-test JSON response and identified per-result duplication that worsens with fleet sweeps
